messages:
noah-peopleops: Quick question 1 1 1 - If someone takes 10 weeks unpaid parental leave, can they make up missed 401k employee deferrals and restore employer match for those missed pay periods after they return?
tanya-eng: I thought employees could do catch-up deferrals subject to IRS limits, but employer match is usually tied to payroll timing.
mike-finance: Short answer: employee can contribute extra up to IRS annual limits, but employer match for missed pay periods is plan-specific. Some plans allow a "make-up" match if set by policy; others do not.
noah-peopleops: Do we have a vendor precedent? has benefits@redwood seen requests like this?
benefits@redwood: We get this occasionally. For our current recordkeeper, the vendor supports "make-up" arrangements only if pre-authorized by plan sponsor and documented before the leave. Typically, employees can make after-tax catch-up contributions but that does not retroactively trigger company match for missed payrolls unless finance approves a manual correction.
leave-bot: Reminder: file leave and note if you want payroll to hold pre-tax deferrals. Link: https://people.redwood.com/leave-request :white_check_mark:
mike-finance: If an employee wants a manual match make-up, they need manager approval + HR paperwork + finance approval. We'll need to open case with the recordkeeper (case# 2026-0799) to confirm if they will accept retroactive match postings.
tanya-eng: Thanks - good to know. Could we add a note to the benefits FAQ about this so folks aren't surprised?
noah-peopleops: Agreed. I'll draft a short FAQ blurb and add a checklist: 1) discuss with manager, 2) submit leave & payroll hold, 3) request match-makeup with finance+benefits.
benefits@redwood: Please include timeline: vendor confirmation can take 7-10 business days and manual corrections may post on next payroll cycle.
mike-finance: I'll prepare a template approval form for managers.
noah-peopleops: Awesome, thanks everyone :pray:
